<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par69 />{{GHGmargin-letter|69|o}}
2. The {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}} frequently has the lengthening by {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁבָה|translate=sit thou}}, {{GHGheb|text=רְדָה|translate=descend thou}}. From {{GHGheb|text=יָהַב|translate=to give}}, Arab. ''wăhăbă'', only the {{GHGterm|imperative}} is used in Hebrew; it has the form {{GHGheb|text=הַב|translate=give}}, lengthened {{GHGheb|text=תָ֫בָה}} generally with the meaning ''age, go to'', hence in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=3.4}} even addressed to several persons ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבָ֫ה}} before {{GHGheb|text=א}} to avoid the hiatus); {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=15}}, {{GHGterm|Milraʿ}} on the analogy of the plural {{GHGheb|text=הָב֫וּ}} (once in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=הָ֫בוּ}} before the tone-syllable; but cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=3}}), whilst, on the analogy of other ''imperatives Qal'' of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֲבִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֲבוּ}} would be expected.—On {{GHGheb|text=דְּעֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=14}}, cf. {{GHGpar|48|l}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|p}}
3. The {{GHGterm|imperfect}} with {{GHGheb|text=ו}} elided takes ''ă'' in the second syllable, besides the cases mentioned above (under f), also in {{GHGheb|text=תֵּרַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=17}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=48}}) and in the pausal form {{GHGheb|text=יֵלַךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=21}}, &c. (from {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ}}, see x); on {{GHGheb|text=יֵקַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=16}} see above, f. The ''ă'' in the second syllable, when followed by the afformative {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} ({{GHGheb|text=תֵּרַ֫דְנָה}} &c.), is in accordance with the law mentioned above (under c), by which ''ă'' takes the place of ''ĭ'' in a doubly closed syllable. Forms with ''ē'' in the second syllable shorten the ''ē'' to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, when the tone is drawn back (before a tone-syllable or after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֵֽשֶׁב־נָא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=33}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫רֶד}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיּ֫שֶׁב}}; but ''ē'' is retained in an open syllable, even with Milʿel-tone, in {{GHGheb|text=יֵ֫צֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=39}}, in both cases with ''nasog ʾaḥor'', {{GHGpar|29|e}}. The ''pausal'' is either of the form {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּשֵׁב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=1}} or {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּרַ֑ד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=10}}; the 1st pers. sing., whether in or out of pause, is {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵרֵד}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵלֵד}} &c., except {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵלַ֑ךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=10}}, see x.—For {{GHGheb|text=יְיֵדָֽע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=138|verse=6}} (cf. the note above, on b and the analogous cases in {{GHGpar|70|d}}) {{GHGheb|text=יֵידָֽע}} is intended.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|q}}
The {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of the form {{GHGheb|text=יִירַשׁ}} is frequently (especially before afformatives) written defectively, in which case the ''î'' can always be recognized as a long vowel by the {{GHGterm|Metheg}} (see {{GHGpar|16|f}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִֽעֲפוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=30}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִֽגְעוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=23}}; and so always {{GHGheb|text=יִֽרְאוּ|translate=they fear}}, as distinguished from {{GHGheb|text=יִרְאוּ|translate=they see}} (''imperf. Qal'' of {{GHGheb|text=רָאָה}}).—On {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫ישֶׂם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=33|hidebook=1}} ''K<sup>e</sup>th'', and {{GHGheb|text=יִיסָךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=30|verse=32}}, see {{GHGpar|73|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|r}}
From {{GHGheb|text=יָכֹל|translate=to prevail, to be able}}, the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} is {{GHGheb|text=יוּכַל}}, which can only have arisen through a depression of the vowel from {{GHGheb|text=יוֹכַל}} (ground-form ''yaukhal''=''yawkhal''), to distinguish it, according to Qimḥi, from {{GHGheb|text=אוֹכַל}}, just as, according to {{GHGpar|47|b}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶקְטֹל}} is differentiated from {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטֹל}}. Cf. the Arabic ''yauruʿu'' (''yôruʿu'') from ''waruʿa, yauǵalu'' (''yôǵalu'') from ''waǵila'', as also the vulgar Arabic (among towns-people) ''yûṣal'', &c., from ''waṣala''. Others regard {{GHGheb|text=יוּכַל}} as an {{GHGterm|imperfect Hophʿal}} (''he is enabled=he can''), always used instead of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}; cf., however, {{GHGpar|53|u}}.—{{GHGheb|text=וַתּוּכָֽל}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=5}} as 2nd ''sing. fem.'' for {{GHGheb|text=וַתּוּכָֽלִי}}, according to König because the 2nd {{GHGterm|fem.}} had been sufficiently indicated previously.—Further {{GHGheb|text=יוֹרֶה}} or {{GHGheb|text=יֹרֶה}} is to be regarded with M. Lambert ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xxxvii, no. 73) as ''impf. Qal'' (not ''Hiphʿil'') of {{GHGheb|text=יָרָה|translate=to throw, shoot}} (the supposed ''impf. Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=וַנִּירָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=30}} is critically very doubtful). This is shown especially by the passages in which the {{GHGterm|impf.}} {{GHGheb|text=יוֹרֶהּ}} is immediately preceded by the ''imperat. Qal'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=13|verse=17}}) or ''infin. Qal'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=64|verse=5}}), or is followed by the {{GHGterm|participle Qal}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=35|verse=23}}; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=11|verse=24}} by the {{GHGterm|participle Hiphʿil}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|s}}
4. The attenuation of ''ă'' to ''ĭ'' in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} (in a toneless, closed syllable) which is discussed in {{GHGpar|44|d}} (cf. {{GHGpar|64|f}}) occurs in verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} in a few forms of {{GHGheb|text=יָלַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=7}}, &c. (always after {{GHGheb|text=יְ}}), as well as of {{GHGheb|text=יָרַשׁ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וִֽירִשְׁתֶּם}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=17|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=19|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=26|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=31|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (always after {{GHGheb|text=וִי}} for {{GHGheb|text=וְיְ}}). In both cases the attenuation might be explained from the tendency to assimilate the vowels, especially if the initial {{GHGheb|text=יְ}} was pronounced, as in Syriac, like ''i'' ({{GHGpar|47|b}}). In the case of {{GHGheb|text=יָרַשׁ}}, however, a secondary form {{GHGheb|text=יַרֵשׁ}} (cf. {{GHGpar|44|d}}) is probably to be assumed, since in Arabic also the verb is ''wărĭṯă''.
